caps_triggered.evidence: shot-a1-framing-mobile.png (chart, y≈640–860): the axis title 'score out of 100' is drawn over the '100' tick label, and the end-of-line labels '73.6'/'71.8' overlap into one blob and run off the SVG right edge (label x = 596+10 with a 20-unit right margin and 22px mobile font). shot-a1-framing-desktop.png and shot-a1-framing-tablet.png show the same title/tick collision and merged end labels. shot-a2-sampling-mobile.png: 'mean sleep (hours)' overwrites the '8.0' tick. shot-a3-correlation-mobile.png: the title 'sunburn clinic visits / week' is clipped at the top edge. Source: app.js:111 (T=20), :122 (title y=14 vs top tick y=24), :130 (end labels), :195/:200, :261/:269.

Chart disagrees with its displayed statistic in Activity 1: (a) 'Gap as drawn on this axis' (app.js:143 → model.js:29) is computed for a 260-unit plot while the chart draws a 280-unit plot (PB−PT = 300−20), so '4.7 px' is not what is drawn (5.0 units, and ~2.5 CSS px at 360 wide); (b) the min slider is allowed up to 72 (index.html:81, app.js:150) and app.js:126 clamps values into the axis, so at min=72 all six Group B values (71.0–71.8) are drawn flat on the axis line while the stat still reports the unclamped 16.7 px (drawn: 14.9) — verified in Node. Feedback copy app.js:245 says late-library students are 'around two-thirds of everyone leaving the library at 21:00'; the sampler (data.js:67) makes them 302/(302+898/4) ≈ 57% (observed pools 54–59%).

verdict: A well-engineered package — clean data/model/UI split, seeded data with byte-identical exports, 13 real tests passing with the documented command, zero runtime requests, and a Pages preview identical to the source — but the charts fail the lesson's own standard: axis titles overwrite ticks and end-labels collide or clip at all three captured widths, the Activity 1 'gap as drawn' statistic does not match what is drawn (and diverges further when the slider clamps Group B onto the axis), and 16 of 52 Port Lumen weeks are floored to zero so the cool-season r is a censoring artefact. Learner copy also states figures the data do not support ('two-thirds' vs 57%) and the guide claims r is defined on screen when it is not. Fix chart geometry, slider bound and generator and this is a 7 next round.

gap_to_10: Seeing Theory (Brown): there the chart IS the statistic — sample means fall onto the histogram as you draw them, the regression line moves under your cursor, and nothing on screen can contradict anything else, at any width. Here the A1 chart needs a separate 'px' box to tell you what you are looking at and that box can disagree with the picture; the scatter carries a censored pile at the origin that the story never mentions; axis titles and end-labels collide; and the learner's first random draw is chosen by a seed rather than designed to teach. Reaching 10 means the picture itself carries the evidence, the data-generating process is defensible line by line, and the copy quotes only numbers the model computes.
